answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy can hinge on staking: each agent must lock a bond, its jade token deposit, before it can bid for work. The notion that one operator can spin up a thousand free identities is a fable, because every duplicate account must post the same bond. When peers detect that two accounts share one operator, they slash the stake, so the attacker pays capital times the number of fake identities they attempt. This rising cost curve is the bridge between cheap pseudonyms and honest participation: beyond a few clones, the attacker loses more than they can extract.
